nodes.summary: Structural congruence: `|` is commutative and associative with unit `nil`, `ν` extrudes over `|` (lifting the other side, which cannot mention the fresh name), restriction of `nil` is `nil`, nested restrictions commute (swapping the two bound indices), and replication unfolds.
nodes.title: Structural congruence of π-calculus processes

nodes.summary: Shift free variables at or above `cutoff` up by one, e.g. when pushing a process under a binder.
nodes.title: Lifting free de Bruijn indices of a π-calculus name

nodes.summary: Shift free variables of a process, entering binders with an increased cutoff.
nodes.title: Lifting free de Bruijn indices of a π-calculus process

nodes.summary: A channel name: a free channel `const n`, or the `i`-th enclosing binder `var i`.
nodes.title: Channel name in the π-calculus

nodes.summary: Processes of the π-calculus. `inp a p` binds variable `0` in `p`; `nu p` binds variable `0` in `p` as a fresh channel.
nodes.title: Processes of the π-calculus

nodes.summary: Guarded-choice resolution: discard sum branches to reach a guarded process. Transitivity handles nested sums.
nodes.title: Guarded-choice resolution in the π-calculus

nodes.summary: Reduction: communication (substituting the sent channel for the input variable) between any selected output and input guards, reduction under `|` and `ν`, and reduction up to structural congruence.
nodes.title: Reduction relation of the π-calculus

nodes.summary: Substitute the name `n` for the variable at `cutoff`: variables below the cutoff are bound by inner binders and untouched, the variable at the cutoff is replaced by `n`, and variables above shift down by one.
nodes.title: Substitution of a name into a π-calculus name

nodes.summary: Substitution leaves a process with no `var 0` untouched: a constant channel stays constant, and the empty process stays empty.
nodes.title: Substitution leaves constant channels and the empty process unchanged

nodes.summary: Substitute the name `n` for the variable at `cutoff` in a process. Under a binder, `n` is lifted by one at cutoff `0` so it keeps referring to the same outer names: every free index of `n` refers to a binder above the substitution point, so all of them shift. Lifting at the current cutoff would leave indices below the cutoff captured by the new binder.
nodes.title: Substitution of a name into a π-calculus process at a cutoff

nodes.summary: Substitute the name `n` for the innermost bound variable of `p`.
nodes.title: Substitution for the innermost bound variable of a process

nodes.summary: Swap the two de Bruijn indices `cutoff` and `cutoff + 1` in a name: the two binders at that depth exchange places.
nodes.title: Swapping adjacent de Bruijn indices in a name

nodes.summary: Swap the two binders at depth `cutoff` throughout a process, incrementing the cutoff under binders.
nodes.title: Swapping adjacent binders throughout a process

can_prove.label: ready to prove
can_prove.meaning: Statement is in Lean and nothing it needs is blocked, so the proof can start.

can_state.label: ready to state
can_state.meaning: Everything its statement uses is in Lean, so the statement can be written in Lean.

conditional.label: conditionally proved
conditional.meaning: Proof compiles, but rests on an open statement without a recorded Lean proof.

fully_proved.label: fully proved
fully_proved.meaning: Proved, and every prerequisite is fully proved too.

inventory_checked.label: inventory checked
inventory_checked.meaning: Module inventory checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

inventory_pending.label: inventory pending
inventory_pending.meaning: Module inventory not yet checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

not_ready.label: not ready
not_ready.meaning: Needs more blueprint work before it can be attempted.

proved.label: proved
proved.meaning: Proof compiles, but something it rests on is not finished.

stated.label: statement formalized
stated.meaning: Statement is in Lean; the proof is not.
